```{r,echo=F}
options(scipen=999)
pn = function(c,d){
    d = d[c!=0]
    c = c[c!=0]
    p = paste0("{",c,"}x^{",d,"}",collapse="+")
    p = gsub("x^{0}","",p,fixed=T)
    p = gsub("x^{1}","x",p,fixed=T)
    p = gsub("+{-","-{",p,fixed=T)
    p = gsub("+{1}x","+x",p,fixed=T)
    p = gsub("-{1}x","-x",p,fixed=T)
    p = gsub("{-1}x","-x",p,fixed=T)
    p = gsub("{1}x","x",p,fixed=T)
    p = gsub("{","",p,fixed=T)
    p = gsub("}","",p,fixed=T)
    return(p)
}
rat_pairs = list(c(2,3),c(2,5),c(2,7),c(2,9),
                 c(3,2),c(3,4),c(3,5),c(3,7),c(3,8),
                 c(4,3),c(4,5),c(4,7),c(4,9),
                 c(5,2),c(5,3),c(5,4),c(5,6),c(5,7),c(5,8),c(5,9),
                 c(6,5),c(6,7),
                 c(7,2),c(7,3),c(7,4),c(7,5),c(7,6),c(7,8),c(7,9),
                 c(8,3),c(8,5),c(8,7),c(8,9),
                 c(9,2),c(9,4),c(9,5),c(9,7),c(9,8))

mkfrac = function(top,bot){
    if(bot>1){
        return(paste0("\\frac{",top,"}{",bot,"}"))
    } else {
        return(paste0(top))
    }
}
nn = sample(1:length(rat_pairs),1)
rp = rat_pairs[[nn]]
a = rp[1]
b = rp[2]*sample(c(-1,1),1)
frac1 = mkfrac(b,a)
factor1 = pn(c(a,-b),1:0)
badfactor = pn(c(-a,b),1:0)

ach = c(pn(c(a,-b),1:0),
        pn(c(a,b),1:0),
        pn(c(b,a),1:0),
        pn(c(b,-a),1:0))

ach = sample(ach)
al = paste0("* $",ach,"$",collapse="\n")

sol = paste0(1*(ach==factor1))

```

Question
========

Let function $f$ represent a cubic polynomial. One solution to the equation $f(x)=0$ is $x=`r frac1`$. Which of the following is a known factor of $f$?

Answerlist
--------

`r al`

Solution
========

Solutions to $f(x)=0$ correspond to the factors of $f$ equaling zero. So, if a factor of $f$ is $ax+b$, then we know $ax+b=0$, which if we solve for $x$ gives us $x=\frac{-b}{a}$.

If we take this logic backwards, a solution of $x=\frac{c}{d}$ implies $dx-c$ is a factor. In this case, we were told the solution is:

$$x=`r frac1`$$

Which implies that the linear binomial $`r factor1`$ is a factor. We can check that this factor gives that solution by solving $`r factor1`=0$.
